subject: Regional service diversion — immediate reroute steps and follow-up
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@payments-inc.com>, ops@fintech.co
Cc: Alex Chang <alex.chang@cloudbroker.io>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Regional service diversion — immediate reroute steps and follow-up

Hi Marta / Payments Ops team —

Wanted to update you quickly: our monitoring has detected elevated request failures and anonymized token drops for clients routed through our eu-central and apac-south clusters beginning ~08:10 UTC. We’ve identified a cloud provider networking flap affecting those regions that is causing intermittent connection resets and higher tail latency for streaming RPCs.

What we’ve done for you so far:
- Automatic fallback routing enabled for your account to route new connections to us-east-1 while eu/apac recover.
- Deployed a temporary model variant (gpt-redwood-lite) in us-east with pinned quantization to preserve response characteristics.

Immediate recommended actions (minimal code changes):
1) If you can, point traffic at our regional endpoint explicitly: https://api.redwood.ai/v1?region=us-east-1 (header alternative: X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: us-east-1). This avoids cross-region DNS propagation delays.
2) If you use connection pooling, drain sockets to allow new connections to pick up routed endpoints.
3) Increase client-side request timeout by +2s and enable exponential backoff (retry-after jitter) for idempotent requests.
4) For streaming: fall back to short-poll streaming with chunk_size=512 tokens if you observe stalls.

Attachments: regional-reroute-steps.pdf (step-by-step DNS/header examples), incident-timeline-20260509.csv (observability slices).

We’ll keep you updated on timeline estimates; engineering is prioritizing restoring full routing to eu/apac. If you’d like, I can schedule a 20-min bridge with our SRE (Markus) and your ops team to walk through a live reroute.

–Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

From: Marta Ruiz <marta@payments-inc.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional service diversion — immediate reroute steps and follow-up

Thanks Naomi —

Appreciate the quick heads up. A few clarifications:
- We are heavy on EU traffic for EU Card Auth flows. If we send region=us-east-1 will latency spike for EU customers?
- Is the gpt-redwood-lite model behaviorally equivalent for our risk-scoring prompts? We run long context (4k tokens).

We can do the header approach today but want to understand downstream latency impact for EU customers before flipping DNS.

Can we take you up on the 20-min bridge? Ops available 10:30–11:30 PDT.

—Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure, Payments, Inc.
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@payments-inc.com>, ops@fintech.co
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional service diversion — immediate reroute steps and follow-up

On Sat, May 9, 2026 at 09:12, Marta Ruiz <marta@payments-inc.com> wrote:
> Thanks Naomi —
> 
> Appreciate the quick heads up. A few clarifications:
> - We are heavy on EU traffic for EU Card Auth flows. If we send region=us-east-1 will latency spike for EU customers?
> - Is the gpt-redwood-lite model behaviorally equivalent for our risk-scoring prompts? We run long context (4k tokens).

Good questions — short answers first: routing to us-east will add median RTT but in our tests we’ve seen <40–80ms additional network latency vs eu for small requests; for streaming long-context calls the predominant cost is tokenization/compute, not cross-region RTT, because the connection stays open and tokens stream. For most of your auth flows we expect total latency increase within the SLA buffer.

On model parity: gpt-redwood-lite is a compatibility-tuned variant. For >4k contexts we recommend you use the compatibility flag long_context=true (client param) so the runtime uses segmented KV streaming; otherwise, expect some quality delta on very long prompts. If you want exact parity, we can keep routing a subset of traffic to the eu cluster once connectivity stabilizes — we can do a 10% canary to validate.

Bridge: Markus and I can join at 10:45 PDT. Sending a calendar invite now.

—Naomi

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Regional service diversion — immediate reroute steps and follow-up

Forwarding Marta's questions and Naomi's guidance so we have the operational checklist in one place. Action items for engineering/SRE: 
- Confirm timeline for BGP announcement rollback in eu-central and apac-south (ETA and rollback plan).
- Provide a short deck for customers summarizing measurable latency delta (median/p95) for header-based routing vs DNS flip.
- Confirm that gpt-redwood-lite with long_context=true matches tokenization for 4k prompts; if not, list known differences.
- Prep one-line runnable client code snippets for: header routing, timeout bump, and streaming fallback.

Markus — can you own the model-compatibility item? Vanessa — please own the customer comms artifact and the one-page latency table. I’ll attach observability slices and the incident timeline to the HubSpot ticket.

Thanks,
David

Subject: [Post-incident] eu/apac routing restored — next steps and postmortem plan

Hi Marta —

Update: the cloud provider confirmed service stabilization for eu-central/apac-south at ~14:20 UTC on 2026-05-10. We’ve validated routing and restored normal BGP announcements as of 14:48 UTC. Observability shows error rates returned to baseline and tail latencies recovered.

What this means for you:
- If you applied header-based routing to us-east, you can safely revert to default region resolution. No customer-facing change is required; we recommend toggling back during a low-traffic window.
- We will not retroactively change any inference outputs; the small-model canary we used for continuity is consistent with your production signals (see short diff in the attached incident-timeline-20260509.csv).

Postmortem & follow-up items we’ll own and deliver by EOD 2026-05-12:
1) Two-page incident summary for your security/compliance folder (root cause, mitigation timeline, and data-handling notes).
2) Latency comparison table (header routing vs DNS) tailored to your 95th percentile auth flows.
3) Code snippets and a small runbook for ops to switch to header-based routing if needed in future.
4) Offer of a 1:1 review session with our SRE/Performance team to validate any fine-grained perf concerns.

Let us know whether you want the two-page summary in PDF or in a shared Google Doc. I’ll attach the incident files to HubSpot: HS-11245 and flag the account for outreach from Customer Success.

Appreciate your patience and fast coordination — will keep you posted once the postmortem assets are uploaded.

–Naomi
